To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a subset of hnRNPs is lost from the nucleus as cells differentiate, and that this loss correlates with the loss of cell proliferation potential.

the loss of proliferating potential during terminal differentiation is accompanied by a loss in the abundance of a subset hnRNP proteins that are associated with 30-40s substructures of hnRNP complexes.

the loss of proliferation potential coincides with the decrease in abundance of P2P, a subset of heterogeneous nuclear ribonuclear proteins, in two distinct cell types, murine mesenchyme stem cells and human epidermal keratinocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of proteins that are associated with the proliferative potential of cells and that can be used as markers of proliferative potential.
the role of P2Ps in the regulation of cell growth and differentiation.

the characterization of a subset of basic proteins associated with hnRNP complexes that are present in rapidly growing and reversibly growth-ar-rested cells, but are decreased or absent from terminally differentiated and reversibly growth-inhibited cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the loss of proliferating potential during terminal differentiation is associated with a decrease in abundance of the P2Ps.
a subset of highly basic proteins, P2P, are associated with proliferative capacity in cells and that these proteins are associated with hnRNP particles and share an epitope with hsp90.
a correlation exists between the presence or absence of a subset of nuclear proteins in cells and their proliferative potential.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
P2Ps are a subset of heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein complexes and are involved in the control of cell proliferation.
the loss of proliferating potential in association with terminal differentiation is associated with a decrease in the abundance of a subset, but not all, of hnRNP complexes.
the loss of the proliferative potential is accompanied with the decreased abundance and/or altered distribution of a subset of hnRNPs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence or absence of a subset of hnRNPs is associated with the proliferative potential of a cell, whether the cell is actively growing or reversibly arrested.
the loss of proliferating potential in terminally differentiated cells correlates with the decrease in abundance of the P2Ps.

a subset of nuclear proteins that are associated with the hnRNP particles are involved in the regulation of proliferation potential and may mediate post-transcriptional control of specific RNAs that are required for proliferation.
